decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash and Aegislash lead safely scout their Protect-heavy tempo: Rotom resists Make It Rain and threatens Tyranitar, Basculegion, and Arcanine; Aegislash can Wide Guard spreads and King's Shield. Garchomp stays back to avoid early Intimidate/Ice and cleans once Protects are exposed. Overqwil is the pivot for Whimsicott/Gholdengo and late Intimidate.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Prankster Whimsicott Tailwind/Encore/Helping Hand with Focus Sash; Gholdengo Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Protect and Good as Gold blocks status; Milotic Recover/Protect with Competitive punishing Intimidate; Arcanine Intimidate/Extreme Speed; Tyranitar likely Mega with sand, Rock Slide/Ice Punch; Basculegion Adaptability Wave Crash/Aqua Jet/Icy Wind. Expect Tyranitar/Basculegion in decider; Whimsicott likely lead. Plan: Rotom-Wash + Aegislash lead to scout Protect and absorb Make It Rain; Rotom threatens Tyranitar/Basculegion/Arcanine, Aegislash uses Wide Guard vs Rock Slide/Icy Wind/Make It Rain and King's Shield vs single-target physical. Garchomp stays back until Intimidate/Ice pressure is spent; EQ spread is safe with Rotom Levitate, Yache lets it survive one Ice Punch/Icy Wind/Ice Beam. Overqwil is the Whimsicott/Gholdengo pivot: Poison Jab breaks Sash, Aqua Jet finishes, immune Shadow Ball, Crunch hits Gholdengo/Basculegion; avoid switching it into active Milotic because Intimidate triggers Competitive. Aegislash must respect Gholdengo Shadow Ball and Tyranitar Crunch; scout with King's Shield and avoid consecutive Protect. Floette benched because Make It Rain OHKOes it and Whimsicott resists Fairy; Talonflame benched because Power Gem/Rock Slide can KO despite Charti. If future games show Milotic/Tyranitar without Gholdengo, consider Floette Energy Ball/Light of Ruin; if Tailwind becomes unmanageable, consider Talonflame. Primary win condition: Rotom + Garchomp once their Protect structure is exposed; avoid giving Milotic free Recover.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott provides immediate Prankster Tailwind and Encore control, while Milotic actively pressures Garchomp and punishes Intimidate users. Gholdengo preserves strong pressure into Fairy- and Ghost-based threats, and Basculegion supplies a second speed-control option plus physical Water pressure. This composition avoids overcommitting to Tyranitar into Garchomp and Rotom-Wash.
decisions.notebook: Opponent commonly pairs Garchomp Earthquake with Levitate Rotom-Wash; preserve an active way to pressure both rather than relying on repeated Protect. Rotom often uses Thunderbolt into exposed or weakened targets. Aegislash remains an important counterplay constraint because of Wide Guard and King's Shield. Favor immediate speed control and keep Milotic or Basculegion available for Garchomp pressure; keep Gholdengo available for Fairy/Ghost matchups.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt Whimsicott is a 100% Focus Sash breaker; Aegislash Flash Cannon then KOs it, removing Prankster Encore/Tailwind support before Whimsicott can act again. Milotic moves before us under Tailwind but its attacks cannot KO Rotom or Shield Aegislash. This line is more robust than hitting Milotic if Milotic Protects, and avoids leaving Whimsicott at 1 HP to Encore.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash Modest 32HP/32SpA/2SpD: Shield 167/160/162; after any attack it is Blade 167/70/211/72 until King's Shield. King's Shield success resets after an attacking move, so it can safely protect/revert after Flash Cannon/Shadow Ball. Wide Guard blocks Make It Rain, Rock Slide, Icy Wind, Earthquake. Rotom Thunderbolt Whimsicott is the reliable Focus Sash breaker; Blade Flash Cannon KOs Sash-broken Whimsicott. Rotom Thunderbolt Milotic 50-84%; Blade Shadow Ball Milotic 27-46%; together usually 2HKO through Leftovers unless Protect/Recover. Milotic Scald vs Blade Aegi 45-68, Ice Beam 17-25; neither KOs from full with Leftovers, and burn is offset by Leftovers. Garchomp Yache survives one Milotic Ice Beam 28-64 but usually not a second; keep Garchomp out until Ice pressure is spent or Protect is forced. Overqwil Intimidate triggers Milotic Competitive; avoid switching Overqwil into Milotic unless necessary. Overqwil Poison Jab breaks Whimsicott Sash, Aqua Jet finishes, Crunch hits Gholdengo/Basculegion, Dark/Poison pivots vs Gholdengo. Against Milotic stall, force Protect/Recover, then attack with Rotom Thunderbolt and Aegislash Shadow Ball; consider Garchomp EQ only after Protect is exposed. Tyranitar likely Mega sand; Rotom threatens Tyranitar/Basculegion/Arcanine, Aegislash walls Fairy/Steel and scouts with King's Shield. If Tailwind becomes unmanageable in future games, consider Talonflame; if Milotic/Tyranitar without Gholdengo, Floette can be considered.

decisions.rationale: Set Tailwind immediately to secure speed control and enable the backline against the broader roster. Milotic uses Scald into Aegislash for direct damage and a burn chance, while avoiding the weaker Ice Beam/Rotom line. This preserves both future Garchomp pressure and Gholdengo's Fairy/Ghost utility.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is the preferred opening speed-control plan. Preserve Basculegion for Garchomp pressure and Gholdengo for Fairy/Ghost matchups. Respect Rotom-Wash Thunderbolt into Milotic and Aegislash's Wide Guard/King's Shield sequencing.

decisions.rationale: Switch Whimsicott’s slot to Gholdengo to maintain immediate offensive pressure against Aegislash while preserving Basculegion for future Garchomp pressure. Milotic should pass and avoid exposing itself to another Thunderbolt.

Gholdengo Shadow Ball OHKOes Blade Aegislash and can heavily damage Rotom; Milotic can add chip, so attacking unprotected risks losing Rotom or Aegislash. First-use Protect and King's Shield are guaranteed, block all likely attacks, revert Aegislash to Shield, and burn one Tailwind turn. This preserves both Pokemon and forces the opponent to reveal or commit before we attack.

reflections.summary: The decider was won by the Rotom-Wash and Garchomp core: Rotom pressured Gholdengo, Garchomp's Earthquake removed it, Thunderbolt eliminated Basculegion, and Electric/Ground pressure eventually broke Milotic despite Protect. The final plan of removing Gholdengo first and finishing Milotic with Thunderbolt helped win the series. The preview plan was imperfect: Aegislash was an unsafe Gholdengo answer and died early, Overqwil was unused, and no Mega was evolved, but Rotom-Wash and Garchomp carried the matchup.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, keep Rotom-Wash and Garchomp as the core but reconsider Aegislash and Overqwil in the four. Bring a safer Gholdengo answer than Modest Leftovers Aegislash, likely considering Spiritomb from the left-behind pool, and avoid giving Milotic free Competitive boosts from Intimidate. Keep Yache Garchomp for Ice Beam, prioritize Thunderbolt over Hydro Pump when accuracy matters, and only bring a Mega if it directly answers Gholdengo or Milotic.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore support, Gholdengo special pressure with Protect, Milotic stall via Scald/Recover/Protect and Competitive, and Basculegion Adaptability water priority. They use Protect frequently and punish Intimidate with Milotic. Rotom-Wash Levitate makes Garchomp Earthquake safe; Thunderbolt is the reliable Milotic/Basculegion finisher; Hydro Pump is useful for chunking Gholdengo but less reliable as a closer. Aegislash is not a safe Gholdengo answer after burn and Shadow Ball pressure. Overqwil is risky into Milotic. Prep conclusion: build around Rotom-Wash + Garchomp, bring a sturdier Gholdengo switch-in, and keep Electric coverage for Milotic/Basculegion.

reflections.summary: Lost the game and series 1-2 primarily because the brought four lacked reliable speed control and had poor defensive positioning into Rotom-Wash plus Garchomp. Rotom's Thunderbolt repeatedly invalidated Milotic and Basculegion, while Garchomp's Earthquake pressured both slots and eventually finished the game. The plan did get useful results—Gholdengo removed Aegislash and Ice Beam consumed Yache Berry—but it could not convert those gains. No between-game adjustment is evidenced, so it cannot be credited with helping; the decisive issue was the team-preview choice and matchup plan rather than execution errors. Bringing Whimsicott without successfully using Tailwind, and bringing both Milotic and Basculegion into Rotom-Wash, was poorly suited. Not evolving a Mega was also questionable; Mega Tyranitar or an Arcanine-based mode should have been seriously considered. The supplied evidence does not establish that Tauros, Lopunny, Furfrou, or Chimecho would definitely have been better, nor does it provide their sets, but the registered six and their demonstrated sets did not sufficiently answer this opponent.
reflections.adjustment: Against a rematch, do not default to the same four. Prioritize Whimsicott with an immediate Tailwind plan or another method of speed control, and avoid pairing two Water-types that Rotom-Wash can freely punish. Consider bringing Mega Tyranitar if its built set can pressure Rotom, Aegislash, and the revealed Fairy options, or Arcanine for Intimidate and broader positioning; choose the Mega holder from the preview rather than leaving the Mega unused. Preserve Gholdengo as an Aegislash answer, but support it with partners that do not force repeated Protect/pass turns against Earthquake and Thunderbolt. Attack or switch on the turn after Protect rather than allowing Milotic to remain exposed to the Rotom-Garchomp combination.
reflections.notebook: Rotom-Wash is a durable major threat to weakened Water-types; Thunderbolt was repeatedly targeted into them, while Hydro Pump also pressured Gholdengo. Garchomp carries Earthquake, Dragon Claw, Iron Head, Protect, and Yache Berry; once Yache is consumed, Ice pressure is much stronger, but it still threatens both slots with spread Earthquake. Aegislash carried Shadow Ball, Flash Cannon, Wide Guard, and King's Shield; Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is an effective direct answer. Talonflame revealed Tailwind, Brave Bird, Flare Blitz, and Quick Guard, so priority-dependent plans and unprotected setup are vulnerable. Floette-Eternal is a Mega user with Moonblast, Light of Ruin, Energy Ball, and Protect; Overqwil has Intimidate and priority Aqua Jet. Future preparation should include a concrete speed-control plan, a Ground/Electric-safe core, and a way to pressure Rotom without relying on Water-types. Reconsider the four selected and use the available Mega slot when it improves the matchup; do not repeat a passive Water-heavy composition merely because Basculegion can threaten Garchomp. The prior plan correctly identified Garchomp as an Ice target and Aegislash as a Gholdengo target, but it underestimated Rotom's ability to invalidate the chosen defensive backbone.
